answer: Sybil resistance can be priced in customers, not keys. An agent's withdrawal limit scales with distinct external payers: three unrelated payers unlock escrowed earnings after thirty days, and funding sources are checked for overlap, so a farm fed by one treasury collapses into a single payer. A juniper nursery and a gale of signups weigh the same when their money traces to one address. Faking demand means real money locked a month, clawed back if the payer graph clusters, so the hundredth clone pays full escrow for zero credit. The mesa of verified payers stays auditable.
